title: Region chooser: weighted latency & capacity fallback orchestration
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Problem statement: As traffic grows across regions we observe periodic hotspots (short-lived capacity pressure) and longer-term latency divergence between regions. Current steering uses a simple latency threshold + geo preference which leads to either (a) excessive cross-region hedging and higher cost or (b) aggressive geo pinning that breaches latency SLOs when a pinned region degrades. Goal: implement a Region Chooser that combines weighted, smoothed latency signals with live capacity hints and circuit-breaker state to produce per-request routing decisions that: 1) prefer local/regional capacity while 2) allow measured cross-region hedging when local latency is trending toward breach, and 3) gracefully shed or fallback when capacity is constrained. Core design tenets: - SLO-first: routing decisions must be guided by per-tenant/request SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency budgets) and a configurable risk tolerance. - Capacity-aware: use capacity hints (available slots, enqueue depth, GPU util percentile) rather than only downstream latencies to avoid reactive thundering. - Smooth transitions: avoid flapping via hysteresis windows, EWMA of latency, and weight decay for temporary spikes. - Controlled cost: add a tunable cross-region budget (tokens per minute) to bound hedging costs. - Observability & rollout safe: incremental rollout with canary, dominant-metric dashboards, and automatic rollbacks when SLO regressions are detected. Implementation components: - Region score calculation: score(r) = w_latency * normalized_latency_score + w_capacity * normalized_capacity_score + w_cost * normalized_cost_penalty + w_affinity * affinity_score. Normalization and weight defaults included in the design doc below. - Circuit breaker states per region and per-model variant: CLOSED | PROBING | OPEN, with transitions driven by combined error ratios, queue growth, and sustained latency above configured SLO windows. - Hedging policy: allow speculative sends to 1 fallback region when predicted SLO violation probability crosses a threshold; hedges limited by budget tokens. - Load shedding: token-bucket based shedding at the ingress tier respecting request priority and customer tier; shedding emits structured reason codes. - Runtime knobs: per-customer SLO override, per-route affinity rules, max-cross-region-per-minute, prefer-local-scale factor. Tasks: 1) Spec the full scoring function and default weights (this ticket). 2) Implement scoring + decisions in request director (C++ runtime). 3) Add metrics (explained below) and dashboard. 4) E2E canary + progressive rollout with performance experiments. 5) Update rollout playbook and SLO alerting to include routing-induced regressions. Deliverables: spec, unit + integration tests, load test report, rollout runbook, PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring spec merged in docs repo with examples and default weights
Request director implements scoring and returns deterministic decisions in unit tests
Circuit-breaker transitions exercised by synthetic failure tests (CLOSED->OPEN->PROBING->CLOSED) and logged with reason codes
Load tests show no >5% increase in median cost for hedging enabled scenarios compared to baseline
Canary rollout plan validated: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% traffic with automated rollback on p95 SLO regression >5%
telemetry: per-region capacity hint metrics (free_slots, enqueue_depth, gpu_util_p90)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: unit and integration tests + staging experiment (all traffic from us-west->eu-west synthetic) Phase 2: internal canary (internal customers) 0.1% traffic 48h -> evaluate metrics Phase 3: public canary 1% 72h -> 10% 72h -> 100% with automated rollback thresholds. Rollback triggers: sustained p95 SLO regression >5% over baseline for 1h OR circuit-breaker opens in >2 regions simultaneously OR hedging budget spend >50% of expected cost budget.
design_notes: Weighting defaults (initial): w_latency=0.6, w_capacity=0.25, w_cost=0.1, w_affinity=0.05. Latency normalization uses sigmoid mapping anchored at tenant SLO: normalized_latency_score = sigmoid((observed_p95 - target_p95) / sensitivity). Capacity score is inverse of enqueue_depth scaled by free_slots. Cost penalty is linear with cross-region expected egress estimate. Hysteresis: require 3 consecutive evaluation ticks (tick=1s) before applying a score-based route change for non-hedging flows. Circuit breaker windows: short-window (30s) for fast failures, long-window (5m) for sustained degradation. Hedging heuristic: only hedge when predicted probability of missing p95 > 0.15 and remote region score delta exceeds local by >0.12. Token buckets per-tenant reset rate configurable in console.
testing_plan: Create synthetic traffic generator to emulate: - cold spike causing increased enqueue_depth - slow model variant causing latency creep - total blackout for a region. Run 4x load test matrices across instance sizes and measure p50/p95/p99, cost, shed_rate. Integration tests will mock capacity hints and assert decision determinism. Add chaos job that simulates region blackouts during canary windows.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Gupta: Initial spec draft posted to Confluence. Requested input from Capacity team on what capacity hints are reliable (free_slots vs available_inflight).
2026-02-25 - Miguel Santos: Implemented prototype in request-director branch 'region-chooser-proto'. Pushed early bench harness. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1823

2026-03-02 - Capacity team (Claire Chen): free_slots is available via exporter but currently 10s granularity. enqueue_depth is real-time but noisy; suggested smoothing window. Recommend using both with weight favoring free_slots for stability.

2026-03-05 - Load test (staging): observed 12% p95 regression in eu-west under hedging-on with default weights. Hypothesis: hedge threshold too low and causes premature cross-region hedges. Action: increase hedge threshold and add cost_penalty weight.
2026-03-08 - Design review (PM: Jordan Patel): approved metric set and rollout plan. Requested per-tenant emergency-turnoff flag in Console. Added as follow-up task.
2026-03-10 - Miguel Santos: Updated scoring function defaults and landed CR with test harness. Next: gated canary after infra approves token-bucket implementation.
